author: EmuCore - Hub
title: Install and troubleshoot PS2 texture replacements
summary: Match a texture pack to the exact title and dump naming, keep replacements outside the game image, control memory pressure, and isolate missing or incorrect textures with logging.
heroAlt: A PCSX2 texture-replacement comparison before enhanced textures are applied

blocks.text: Replacements are external assets keyed to game textures

A texture pack does not increase internal resolution and should not rewrite the disc image. The renderer identifies textures during play and substitutes external PNG or DDS-style assets according to the implementation's naming rules. Packs can be region/revision sensitive, consume far more memory than original textures and conflict with dumping mode or another pack.
Keep the original game image untouched and install one pack at a time. Back up the game's texture folder before merging or renaming files.

Verify the game serial/CRC and read the pack's supported revision, renderer and folder instructions. Check archive structure before extraction; reject archives that contain executables or unrelated emulator configuration. Start with native or modest resolution and the system driver to preserve memory headroom.

items: Verified title identity and supported pack revision.
Traceable pack source and archive hash.
Enough free storage and RAM/GPU memory headroom.
Backup of any existing texture folder.
Texture dumping disabled for the first replacement test.
1. Inspect the archive and identify its documented game folder rather than extracting directly into the emulator-data root.
2. Import through EmuCoreX's texture manager or place the folder in the exact managed location while emulation is stopped.
3. Enable texture replacement for the target game only and cold-boot a scene named by the pack author.
4. Watch logs for loaded/rejected textures and inspect UI, gameplay, FMV and transitions for wrong substitutions.
5. Run a warm memory-pressure test, then disable the pack and confirm the baseline returns without changing the image hash.

blocks.text: A working pack replaces expected assets consistently across two boots, shows no unrelated images, and remains within storage/memory limits. Texture dumping should go to a separate workflow; leaving it enabled while playing can create large folders and make it unclear whether a file is source or replacement.

items: Folder identity matches title serial/CRC.
Expected textures load in two cold runs.
No unrelated or transparent textures are substituted.
Long session avoids out-of-memory or driver resets.
Disabling the pack restores the original visuals.

blocks.text: Disable replacement, stop emulation and restore the previous texture folder from backup. Remove the newest pack as a whole rather than deleting files by guess after a merge. If memory errors persist, clear only the pack-specific cache and retest the original baseline.

items: Disable the target game's texture replacement.
Restore the pre-install texture directory.
Remove merged/unknown files by replacing the whole working folder.
Return resolution and driver to the recorded baseline.
Some textures never change: names or game revision do not match.
Wrong image appears on objects: pack contains collision or foreign-title files.
Crash after several areas: memory pressure or oversized assets.
Storage grows continuously: dumping remained enabled.

blocks.text: Keep each pack in its own versioned archive with source, hash and supported game identity. A clean install and whole-folder rollback are more reliable than gradually merging community packs until nobody can identify which asset produced a fault.
